scenarios.title: Protect hosted media quota and incomplete uploads
plannedActions: Finish all original checks and save the original team/memberships; set the synthetic team quota to 12.
Upload a 12-byte PNG, verify exact row/object/quota, retry unchanged and read public team storageUsed=12.
Refuse distinct 3-byte JPEG at full quota without mutation. Delete PNG, upload the same JPEG successfully, delete it twice and read public storageUsed=0.

For logout case, seed fresh synthetic member with attempt and retained sessions. Hold a PNG PUT after one body byte. Observe fresh request/upload markers at one, then publicly log out attempt session and verify revocation while retained session remains live.

Release the body and require exact 409/upload_unavailable with exact storage/quota preservation. Require old-token identity read 401, then upload identical bytes with retained session, verify exact replica and delete as owner.

For downgrade case, seed another fresh member/session, hold the same valid PNG PUT and observe both markers. Publicly change member to viewer, verify stored role and still-live session, then release body and require exact 409 and storage preservation.

Attempt a fresh viewer upload and require exact 402 without upload-counter increment; publicly restore member and verify stored role. Retry identical upload with the same session, verify exact replica and delete as owner.

Restore original storage_limit, compare the complete original team row and original membership rows, require two added fixture memberships only, empty media, 20 added HTTP requests and zero outbound attempts.
expectedOutcomes: With only the synthetic team storage_limit set to 12 and no media present, a 12-byte PNG reaches exact quota and a duplicate retry preserves every row/object/team field. Public team read reports 12. A distinct 3-byte JPEG receives exact 413/storage_quota with all state unchanged. Deleting PNG frees quota, JPEG then uploads successfully, and deleting it twice leaves zero storage and no media; public read reports zero.

For two fresh synthetic upload users, send only the first PNG byte under exact Content-Length. A fresh upload counter at one proves initial project/premium/write authorization passed; the session request counter is also one. Before any response or body release, publicly log out one attempt session or downgrade the other user to viewer. Complete the body only after verifying that state change. Both held writes return exact 409/upload_unavailable without asset, object or team/quota changes.

After refused held writes, the revoked token receives exact 401 without changing its request marker; a fresh viewer PUT receives exact 402 before changing its upload marker. Retained-session retry after logout and same-session retry after public role restoration each create the exact ready PNG row/R2 bytes/metadata at quota 12. Owner deletion removes it and releases quota. The final original team row and original memberships are restored/preserved; media is empty, 20 new requests finish and unexpected outbound attempts remain zero.

associations.rationale: The real insert trigger rejects 12+3 bytes above the fixture limit while accepting exactly 12. No default 10 GiB-scale or concurrent insert test.
